subject.title: [Feature]: Two-tier agent capabilities: session self-service tools + OpenClaw system-agent delegation (Crestodian rename)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed permanent authority boundary: agents directly manage only their own session-scoped state, while all persistent system changes require delegation to the OpenClaw system agent and explicit human approval?
rationale: This choice changes the security model, default tool authority, public CLI and protocol behavior, provider fallback policy, and upgrade expectations; source inspection can evaluate mechanics but cannot choose the intended permanent product boundary.

options.title: Approve phased two-tier boundary
options.body: Proceed phase by phase with compatibility migrations, scoped session permissions, and explicit approval proof for every persistent system write.

options.title: Ship session self-service only
options.body: Add the bounded session tools while deferring system-agent delegation and gateway-write removal until their security and compatibility contracts are separately approved.

options.title: Retain current gateway authority
options.body: Keep direct gateway writes available by default and treat the system agent as an optional convenience rather than the mandatory persistent-write boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve phased two-tier boundary
recommendation.body: Proceed phase by phase with compatibility migrations, scoped session permissions, and explicit approval proof for every persistent system write.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue and active phase-0 implementation originate from @steipete, who repository guidance identifies as the primary project decision owner.
